reason: Control: a closed, well-formed narrative in the XHTML namespace.

A closing tag that does not match the open element is a parse failure: Found "" expecting "

".
The same, with an inline element: the mismatch is what fails, not the element.

A second p inside the first leaves one open, so meets

.
An element left open where the text ends is taken as closed; the root included.
Two elements left open at the end, with content: still well-formed to this parser.
Bare text under an unclosed root: content, no finding.
The text ends inside a start tag: the element is kept, so the narrative is empty — txt-2 alone, no parse failure.
The same truncation after real content: nothing is reported at all.
The text ends inside a quoted attribute value: what was read is the value.
The text ends just after an attribute's '=': tolerated like any other truncated start tag.
A truncated root start tag keeps its xmlns, so the namespace passes and only txt-2 fails.
A truncated root start tag with no xmlns: the element exists with no namespace, so the namespace finding stands beside txt-2.
The one truncation refused: a '/' no '>' follows — unexpected non-end of element.
The text ends inside a closing tag: Unexpected termination of html source.
The same inside the root's closing tag, after content: the parse failure stands alone and leaves no document, so txt-2 fails too.
A bare '<' at the end: a name is expected, so the node has unexpected content.
A start tag whose next character can begin no attribute name: Unable to read attribute.
The same with a punctuation character: the message names the element, not the character.
An external image source over http is accepted: nothing fetches it, and no scheme check applies to an image.
The same over https.
A path-only image source is accepted; what it would resolve against is not the narrative's business.
A file: image source is accepted — the scheme rules are for hyperlinks only.
urn: in an image source passes, where urn: in a hyperlink is 'not a valid hyperlinkable scheme'.
cid: in an image source passes, for the same reason.
javascript: in an image source passes — the active-content check is a hyperlink check. A host that wants this refused sets externalNarrativeLinks.
vbscript: in an image source likewise passes.
A data: image source needs only its comma.
A data: URL with no comma has no data: the URL is not valid.
An empty image source is an invalid URL (and, unlike a hyperlink, carries no second finding).
A '#' image source that names no id in the narrative, no contained resource and not the resource itself does not resolve.
The same fragment resolving to an id inside the narrative.
A '#' image source naming the resource's own id resolves.
An external hyperlink over http is accepted, for contrast with the image cases.
